name: Brazil Current
scope: Poleward Brazil Current reference route from nominal 14 degrees S origin to nominal 38 degrees S confluence; alternate origins 10/15 degrees S and terminal proxies 34.5/40.5 degrees S. Excludes North Brazil Current, Brazil Return Current recirculation, eastward South Atlantic Current and deep intermediate undercurrent. Confluence-proxy positions are endpoint assumptions, not instantaneous observed axes.
layer: Upper-ocean poleward BC branch geographic reference only. No fixed vertical interval or undercurrent route diagnosed.
time_convention: General geographic sketch using source-described origin and confluence variability. Neither the 2009–2015 mooring period nor the front proxy interval creates a contemporaneous full-current axis.
source_locator: Introduction: SEC bifurcation and BC origin roughly 10–15 degrees S. Southern endpoint convention additionally uses Schmid and Majumder (2018), Sections 3 and 4.3: confluence/front separation proxy varies 34.5–40.5 degrees S and averages near 38 degrees S.
source_citation: Chidichimo et al. (2021), Brazil Current Volume Transport Variability During 2009–2015 From a Long-Term Moored Array at 34.5°S, Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans 126, e2020JC017146.
source_license: Factual geographic references only; no source prose, figures, provider geometry or model data packaged.
coordinate_selection: OSW selects coarse regional offshore waypoints. Sources define flow identity and broad endpoint geography, not these intermediate vertices or longitudes. The path is not a digitized source curve, observed axis, bathymetric contour or diagnosed velocity field.
scenario_rule: Nine paired origin/confluence routes (origins 10/14/15 degrees S; ends 34.5/38/40.5 degrees S) crossed with three uniform longitude shifts (-0.25/0/+0.25 degrees): 27 editorial scenarios. The origin and southern-proxy latitude ranges are source-described; chosen gate longitudes and intermediate vertices are OSW assumptions. This finite envelope is not a statistical interval or an exhaustive meander/seasonal model.
remaining_gates: Independent review of source-specific start/end conventions, branches and seasonal endpoint alternatives.
Check offshore waypoints against reproducible shelf/slope or velocity geometry at suitable resolution.
Canonical claim, geometry and measurement integration before public admission.

supporting_sources.citation: Schmid and Majumder (2018), Transport variability of the Brazil Current from observations and a data assimilation model, Ocean Science 14, 417–436.
supporting_sources.locator: Section 3 (shelf-break path and front separation proxy range) and Section 4.3 (average near 38 degrees S).
supporting_sources.role: Southern endpoint convention and shelf-break route interpretation.
